newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trading slow pre-election.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trading slow pre-election.

text.p: Last week, a string of key economic reports kept many index options participants on the sidelines and this week, Tuesday's presidential elections are doing the same, traders said Monday.

What trading was seen Monday maintained the recent pattern, with put volume outpacing call volume. By 1300 CST (1900 GMT), index puts traded on the CBOE totalled about 81,000 compared to 43,300 index calls.
Analysts said they doubted the market would make a big move in the runup to the election, with most indicators showing a mixed market.
Monday afternoon, most major market indices were higher, led by the S&P 100, which rose 3.88 to 683. The S&P 500 gained 2.55 to 706 and the Dow Industrial average added about 24 to 6,046.
"A lot of people are getting caught up on the day's news," one trader said after spending some time on the floor of the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE). "Nothing's going on."
Traders said activity Tuesday is likely to be sluggish also, with election results not likely until well after the market closes.
Schaeffer said out of the money put open interest in the OEX continues to outpace out of the money call open interest, providing one indication of investor nervousness.
Another such signal is the recent pattern in the CBOE's volatility index, he said.
Last Friday, the VIX dipped only slightly despite the passing of the key October employment report. In past months, the VIX has fallen sharply after the jobs report.
The VIX, down 0.65 at 18.78 Monday afternoon, is also suggesting investor's caution remains high, Schaeffer said.

"From this perspective, a sharp rally in th eVIX between now and Tuesday's close, particularly if the market holds its own, could be a good indicator of speculator nervousness going into the election," Schaeffer said in the report.
That "would imply that the market will tend to react favorably to just about any result short of a Democratic sweep," he said.
